classification.difficultyReason: Introduce a common perpendicular that bisects both concentric chords, use the inner right triangle to find its distance from the centre, then use the outer triangle and double its half-chord.

content.prompt: The figure shows two concentric circles, centre $O$. $OL = 13\text{ cm}$, $OK = 15\text{ cm}$ and $LM = 10\text{ cm}$. Find $KN$.

spec.description: Two concentric circles, common centre O, collinear intersections K, L, M, N, and drawn radii OK and OL. No perpendicular construction is supplied.
spec.mathematics: OL = 13 cm, OK = 15 cm, LM = 10 cm; K and N lie on the outer circle and L and M on the inner circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and point labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $O$ to $KN$. This perpendicular bisects both chords.
$$\begin{align*}LH &= 10\div2=5\text{ cm}\\OH^2 &= 13^2-5^2=144\\OH &= 12\text{ cm}\\KH^2 &= 15^2-12^2=81\\KH &= 9\text{ cm}\\KN &= 2\times9=18\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
